name: Query Doctor
tagline: Diagnose a slow SQL query on Zetaris, rewrite it, and ship the rewrite only when executing both returns the same rows, faster.
feedback_events: Verifier critique (every check), Rewriter retry after REJECT, Diagnoser.revise after NOT_FASTER/no_gain

zetaris.how: Live path: the local Zetaris platform (TPCDS_DB Parquet) over its Lightning JDBC driver through a Java sidecar (engine/zetaris-jdbc/QuerySidecar.java, src/engine/zetaris.ts). The query is run, EXPLAINed (EXPLAIN FORMATTED), row-fingerprinted on the engine (xxhash64) and timed there. The local platform has no MCP endpoint, so none of the four documented MCP tools (get_slow_queries, get_query_stats, profile_table, explain_query) is used; their roles are filled by pasted SQL, SQL aggregates, EXPLAIN and our own wall-clock timing (docs/DX-REPORT.md).

engines: H-MEM (playbook of refused and verified rewrites)
Markovian (rewrite chain, one attempt per chunk)
meterless.nightshift: Implemented as the default model provider (src/adapters/nightshift.ts) and covered by mock-runtime tests. NOT demonstrated against a live Nightshift runtime: every recorded run used the declared fallback (direct NVIDIA NIM, LLM_PROVIDER=nim).

nvidia.how: Diagnoser and Rewriter. Recorded runs reached it directly on NVIDIA's hosted endpoint (provider nim, the declared fallback), not through Nightshift.

cursor.how: cursor-agent wrote the scaffold commit only (d3e823c, trailers Tool: cursor and Co-authored-by: Cursor). Cursor was optional for this event (organiser, 2026-10-22); every other commit was written with Claude Code (Tool: claude-code).

ai_usage.development: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5) wrote 100 of 101 commits; Cursor's agent wrote 1 (the scaffold). Commit trailers record the tool.
ai_usage.review: Code and architecture were reviewed by an outside panel of four models (Qwen, Grok, Codex, Claude Opus); each finding was checked against the code before any change.
ai_usage.runtime: Nemotron 3 Ultra for diagnosis and rewrite proposals. The verdict never comes from a model.
